    47	  decide : QuestionA → QuestionB → AnswerA → AnswerB → Bool
    48	
    49	attribute [instance] Game.questionAFintype Game.questionBFintype
    50	  Game.answerAFintype Game.answerBFintype Game.questionADecidableEq
    51	  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq
    52	
    53	/--
    54	The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
    55	is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation
    57	is the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin
    58	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    59	-/
    60	noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
    61	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    62	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    63	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=
    64	  M.postprocess Prod.fst
    65	
    66	/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in
    67	`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,
    68	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    69	-/
    70	noncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    72	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    73	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=
    74	  M.postprocess Prod.snd
    75	
    76	/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; paper origin
    78	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`). -/
    79	def Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    80	    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=
    81	  ∀ a, IsProj (M.effect a)
    82	
    83	/--
    84	The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in
    85	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69` (paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).
    87	-/
    88	structure Strategy (G : Game) where
    89	  ιA : Type
    90	  ιB : Type
    91	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    92	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    93	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    94	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    95	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    96	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    97	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
    98	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB
    99	
   100	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
   101	  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq
   102	
   103	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   104	the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   110	
   111	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   112	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   113	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   114	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   115	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   117	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   119	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
   120	
   121	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   122	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-48`. -/
   124	noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   125	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   126	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   127	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   128	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   129	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
   130	
   131	/-- Alice's marginal Born weight for an answer at a fixed question. -/
   132	noncomputable def aliceOutcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   133	    (x : G.QuestionA) (a : G.AnswerA) : ℝ :=
   134	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   135	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1
   136	  (inner ℂ S.ψ (applyOperatorToState M S.ψ)).re
   137	
   138	/-- Bob's marginal Born weight for an answer at a fixed question. -/
   139	noncomputable def bobOutcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   140	    (y : G.QuestionB) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   141	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   142	    heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b)
   143	  (inner ℂ S.ψ (applyOperatorToState M S.ψ)).re
   144	
   145	/-- The Born weight of a decidable event on the two answers at fixed questions. -/
   146	noncomputable def outcomeEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   147	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   148	    (E : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] : ℝ :=
   149	  ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   150	    if E a b then outcomeWeight S x y a b else 0
   151	
   152	/-- The marginal Born weight of a decidable event on Alice's answer. -/
   153	noncomputable def aliceEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   154	    (x : G.QuestionA) (E : G.AnswerA → Prop) [DecidablePred E] : ℝ :=
   155	  ∑ a : G.AnswerA, if E a then aliceOutcomeWeight S x a else 0
   156	
   157	/-- The marginal Born weight of a decidable event on Bob's answer. -/
   158	noncomputable def bobEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   159	    (y : G.QuestionB) (E : G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidablePred E] : ℝ :=
   160	  ∑ b : G.AnswerB, if E b then bobOutcomeWeight S y b else 0
   161	
   162	/-- Every answer-pair Born weight is nonnegative.  This is formalization-only
   163	support for the probability expression in `def:tensor-product-value`. -/
   164	theorem outcomeWeight_nonneg {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   165	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) :
   166	    0 ≤ outcomeWeight S x y a b := by
   167	  unfold outcomeWeight applyOperatorToState heteroKron
   168	  exact
   169	    (Matrix.isPositive_toEuclideanLin_iff.mpr
   170	      (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp
   171	        (kronecker_nonneg ((S.A x).pos a) ((S.B y).pos b)))).re_inner_nonneg_right S.ψ
   172	
   173	/-- The Born weights of all answer pairs at fixed questions sum to one.  This
   174	is formalization-only support for the POVM normalization implicit in
   175	`def:tensor-product-value`. -/
   176	theorem outcomeWeight_sum_eq_one {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   177	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) :
   178	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b = 1 := by
   179	  have hsum :
   180	      (∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   181	        heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) =
   182	          (1 : Op (S.ιA × S.ιB)) := by
   183	    ext i j
   184	    simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
   185	      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
   186	    simp_rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_mul]
   187	    rw [show (∑ a : G.AnswerA, (S.A x).effect a i.1 j.1) =
   188	        (1 : Op S.ιA) i.1 j.1 by
   189	      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.A x).sum_eq_one i.1) j.1]
   190	    rw [show (∑ b : G.AnswerB, (S.B y).effect b i.2 j.2) =
   191	        (1 : Op S.ιB) i.2 j.2 by
   192	      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.B y).sum_eq_one i.2) j.2]
   193	    exact congrFun (congrFun
   194	      (Matrix.one_kronecker_one (m := S.ιA) (n := S.ιB) (α := ℂ)) i) j
   195	  calc
   196	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b =
   197	        (inner ℂ S.ψ
   198	          (applyOperatorToState
   199	            (∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   200	              heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
   201	          simp [outcomeWeight, applyOperatorToState]
   202	    _ = (inner ℂ S.ψ (applyOperatorToState 1 S.ψ)).re := by rw [hsum]
   203	    _ = 1 := by
   204	      simp [applyOperatorToState, S.ψ_norm]
   205	
   206	/-- Summing over Bob's answers gives Alice's marginal Born weight. -/
   207	theorem sum_outcome_weight_right {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   208	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) :
   209	    (∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b) = aliceOutcomeWeight S x a := by
   210	  have hsum :
   211	      (∑ b : G.AnswerB, heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) =
   212	        heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1 := by
   213	    ext i j
   214	    simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
   215	      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
   216	    rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
   217	    rw [show (∑ b : G.AnswerB, (S.B y).effect b i.2 j.2) =
   218	        (1 : Op S.ιB) i.2 j.2 by
   219	      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.B y).sum_eq_one i.2) j.2]
   220	  calc
   221	    (∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b) =
   222	        (inner ℂ S.ψ
   223	          (applyOperatorToState
   224	            (∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   225	              heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
   226	          simp [outcomeWeight, applyOperatorToState]
   227	    _ = (inner ℂ S.ψ
   228	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1) S.ψ)).re := by
   229	      rw [hsum]
   230	    _ = aliceOutcomeWeight S x a := rfl
   231	
   232	/-- Summing over Alice's answers gives Bob's marginal Born weight. -/
   233	theorem sum_outcome_weight_left {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   234	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (b : G.AnswerB) :
   235	    (∑ a : G.AnswerA, outcomeWeight S x y a b) = bobOutcomeWeight S y b := by
   236	  have hsum :
   237	      (∑ a : G.AnswerA, heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) =
   238	        heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b) := by
   239	    ext i j
   240	    simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
   241	      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
   242	    rw [← Finset.sum_mul]
   243	    rw [show (∑ a : G.AnswerA, (S.A x).effect a i.1 j.1) =
   244	        (1 : Op S.ιA) i.1 j.1 by
   245	      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.A x).sum_eq_one i.1) j.1]
   246	  calc
   247	    (∑ a : G.AnswerA, outcomeWeight S x y a b) =
   248	        (inner ℂ S.ψ
   249	          (applyOperatorToState
   250	            (∑ a : G.AnswerA,
   251	              heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
   252	          simp [outcomeWeight, applyOperatorToState]
   253	    _ = (inner ℂ S.ψ
   254	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
   255	      rw [hsum]
   256	    _ = bobOutcomeWeight S y b := rfl
   257	
   258	/-- Every answer event has nonnegative Born weight. -/
   259	theorem outcome_event_weight_nonneg {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   260	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   261	    (E : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] :
   262	    0 ≤ outcomeEventWeight S x y E := by
   263	  unfold outcomeEventWeight
   264	  exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => by
   265	    split_ifs
   266	    · exact outcomeWeight_nonneg S x y a b
   267	    · exact le_rfl
   268	
   269	/-- An answer event depending only on Alice has its Alice marginal weight. -/
   270	theorem outcome_event_weight_left_eq {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   271	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   272	    (E : G.AnswerA → Prop) [DecidablePred E] :
   273	    outcomeEventWeight S x y (fun a _ => E a) = aliceEventWeight S x E := by
   274	  unfold outcomeEventWeight aliceEventWeight
   275	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   276	  intro a _
   277	  by_cases ha : E a
   278	  · simp [ha, sum_outcome_weight_right S x y a]
   279	  · simp [ha]
   280	
   281	/-- An answer event depending only on Bob has its Bob marginal weight. -/
   282	theorem outcome_event_weight_right_eq {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   283	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   284	    (E : G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidablePred E] :
   285	    outcomeEventWeight S x y (fun _ b => E b) = bobEventWeight S y E := by
   286	  unfold outcomeEventWeight bobEventWeight
   287	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   288	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   289	  intro b _
   290	  by_cases hb : E b
   291	  · simp [hb, sum_outcome_weight_left S x y b]
   292	  · simp [hb]
   293	
   294	/-- Inclusion of answer events implies the corresponding Born-weight inequality. -/
   295	theorem outcome_event_weight_mono {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   296	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   297	    (E F : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] [DecidableRel F]
   298	    (hEF : ∀ a b, E a b → F a b) :
   299	    outcomeEventWeight S x y E ≤ outcomeEventWeight S x y F := by
   300	  unfold outcomeEventWeight
   301	  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   302	  intro a _
   303	  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   304	  intro b _
   305	  by_cases hE : E a b
   306	  · simp [hE, hEF a b hE]
   307	  · simp only [hE, ↓reduceIte]
   308	    split_ifs
   309	    · exact outcomeWeight_nonneg S x y a b
   310	    · exact le_rfl
   311	
   312	/--
   313	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   314	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   315	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   316	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   317	-/
   318	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   319	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
   320	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   321	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
   322	
   323	/--
   324	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
   325	strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
   326	for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
   327	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin
   328	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is
   329	intentionally not asserted here.
   330	-/

     5	/-!
     6	# Distribution infrastructure for the low individual degree test
     7	
     8	Shared distribution definitions: finite-support weighted distributions,
     9	a probability predicate, push-forward distributions, weighted-sum linear maps,
    10	averaging, uniform distribution, and outcome summation.
    11	
    12	Note: this module contributes declarations to the comparator statement closure
    13	of `mainFormal`, which must elaborate in the same environment as the
    14	Mathlib-only `Challenge.lean`.  Keep the full `import Mathlib`; do not narrow
    15	it.  See `docs/comparator.md`, "Environment alignment".
    16	-/
    17	
    18	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    21	
    22	/-- A finite-support weighted distribution with nonnegative real-valued weights. -/
    23	structure Distribution (α : Type*) where
    24	  support : Finset α := ∅
    25	  weight : α → Error := fun _ => 0
    26	  nonnegative : ∀ a, 0 ≤ weight a := by intro _; positivity
    27	  outsideSupport : ∀ a, a ∉ support → weight a = 0 := by intro _ _; rfl
    28	
    29	namespace Distribution
    30	
    31	/-- The total mass carried by the explicit support of a distribution. -/
    32	def totalWeight {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Error :=
    33	  ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a
    34	
    35	/-- A `Distribution` is probabilistic when its total mass is exactly `1`. -/
    36	def IsProbability {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Prop :=
    37	  𝒟.totalWeight = 1
    38	
    39	/-- Push a finite-support distribution forward along a map.
    40	
    41	This is the project `Distribution` analogue of `PMF.map`.  The support is the
    42	image of the original finite support, and each new weight is the sum of the
    43	weights in the corresponding fiber. -/
    44	noncomputable def map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    45	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) : Distribution β where
    46	  support := 𝒟.support.image e
    47	  weight := fun b => ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a
    48	  nonnegative := fun _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a
    49	  outsideSupport := fun _ hb =>
    50	    Finset.sum_eq_zero fun a ha =>
    51	      (hb (Finset.mem_image.mpr
    52	        ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).1, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩)).elim
    53	
    54	@[simp]
    55	theorem map_support {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    56	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    57	    (𝒟.map e).support = 𝒟.support.image e := rfl
    58	
    59	@[simp]
    60	theorem map_weight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    61	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (b : β) :
    62	    (𝒟.map e).weight b =
    63	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a := rfl
    64	
    65	/-- Push-forward preserves total mass. -/
    66	theorem map_totalWeight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    67	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    68	    (𝒟.map e).totalWeight = 𝒟.totalWeight := by
    69	  simpa [totalWeight, map] using
    70	    (Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    71	      (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)

## Local Operations

This repository runs its whole workflow locally. The short version every
agent must know:

- **Build reuse.** A hot main cache lives under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/`;
  fresh worktrees get it via `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` (which also
  installs git hooks and resets dirty vendored packages). Never run
  `lake update`; never write to the cache; at most one full `lake build`
  runs machine-wide (the scripts take the lock for you).
- **Lifecycle.** GitHub issue → branch `issue-<number>-slug` + worktree →
  agent sessions → `local/bin/ci.sh` → `local/bin/review.sh` → optional
  `local/bin/autofix.sh` → `local/bin/pr_merge.py`. CI and review evidence are
  exact-head commit statuses (`local-ci/*`, `local-review/summary`); merges go
  through GitHub with an exact-SHA guard. Details: `local/README.md`,
  `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`.
- **Sessions.** Dispatch, resume, and archive agent sessions only via
  `local/bin/dispatch.sh` (roles: orc, prover, reviewer, simplifier,
  blueprint, splitter, scout) so token/time telemetry stays complete.
- **Telemetry duty.** Incidents go to `results/telemetry/events.md`;
  protocol changes follow `local/protocols/meta.md` and are ledgered in
  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.
- **Fix commits**: `autofix.sh`'s automated commits are prefixed
  `[codex-auto-fix]` / `[codex-review-fix]` exactly (the review skip keys on
  them); operator and worker repairs use plain `fix(review): …` /
  `fix(ci): …` subjects so they are reviewed. Issue titles, slugs, and branch
  names stay bracket-free.

## Practical Defaults for Agents

When editing Lean code:

1. Read the paper source
2. Read the target Lean file and nearby supporting files
3. Type-check the single file
4. Scan for `sorry|axiom`
5. Run `lake build` only when the local change is stable

When editing blueprint files:

1. Read the matching paper source and chapter file
2. Update Lean links carefully
3. Run `leanblueprint web`

    54	The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
    55	is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation
    57	is the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin
    58	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    59	-/
    60	noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
    61	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    62	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    63	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=
    64	  M.postprocess Prod.fst
    65	
    66	/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in
    67	`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,
    68	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    69	-/
    70	noncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    72	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    73	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=
    74	  M.postprocess Prod.snd

    76	/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; paper origin
    78	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`). -/
    79	def Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    80	    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=

    82	
    83	/--
    84	The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in
    85	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69` (paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).
    87	-/
    88	structure Strategy (G : Game) where
    89	  ιA : Type
    90	  ιB : Type
    91	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    92	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    93	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    94	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    95	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    96	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    97	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
    98	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB
    99	
   100	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
   101	  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq
   102	
   103	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   104	the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   110	
   111	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   112	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   113	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   114	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   115	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   117	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   119	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
   120	
   121	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   122	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-48`. -/
   124	noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   125	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   126	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   127	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   128	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   129	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
   130	
   131	/-- Alice's marginal Born weight for an answer at a fixed question. -/
   132	noncomputable def aliceOutcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   133	    (x : G.QuestionA) (a : G.AnswerA) : ℝ :=
   134	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   135	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1
   136	  (inner ℂ S.ψ (applyOperatorToState M S.ψ)).re
   137	
   138	/-- Bob's marginal Born weight for an answer at a fixed question. -/
   139	noncomputable def bobOutcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   140	    (y : G.QuestionB) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   141	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   142	    heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b)
   143	  (inner ℂ S.ψ (applyOperatorToState M S.ψ)).re
   144	
   145	/-- The Born weight of a decidable event on the two answers at fixed questions. -/
   146	noncomputable def outcomeEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   147	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   148	    (E : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] : ℝ :=
   149	  ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   150	    if E a b then outcomeWeight S x y a b else 0
   151	
   152	/-- The marginal Born weight of a decidable event on Alice's answer. -/
   153	noncomputable def aliceEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   154	    (x : G.QuestionA) (E : G.AnswerA → Prop) [DecidablePred E] : ℝ :=
   155	  ∑ a : G.AnswerA, if E a then aliceOutcomeWeight S x a else 0
   156	
   157	/-- The marginal Born weight of a decidable event on Bob's answer. -/
   158	noncomputable def bobEventWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   159	    (y : G.QuestionB) (E : G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidablePred E] : ℝ :=
   160	  ∑ b : G.AnswerB, if E b then bobOutcomeWeight S y b else 0
   161	
   162	/-- Every answer-pair Born weight is nonnegative.  This is formalization-only
   163	support for the probability expression in `def:tensor-product-value`. -/
   164	theorem outcomeWeight_nonneg {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   165	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) :
   166	    0 ≤ outcomeWeight S x y a b := by
   167	  unfold outcomeWeight applyOperatorToState heteroKron
   168	  exact
   169	    (Matrix.isPositive_toEuclideanLin_iff.mpr
   170	      (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp
   171	        (kronecker_nonneg ((S.A x).pos a) ((S.B y).pos b)))).re_inner_nonneg_right S.ψ
   172	
   173	/-- The Born weights of all answer pairs at fixed questions sum to one.  This
   174	is formalization-only support for the POVM normalization implicit in
   175	`def:tensor-product-value`. -/
   176	theorem outcomeWeight_sum_eq_one {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   177	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) :
   178	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b = 1 := by
   179	  have hsum :
   180	      (∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   181	        heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) =
   182	          (1 : Op (S.ιA × S.ιB)) := by
   183	    ext i j
   184	    simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
   185	      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
   186	    simp_rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_mul]
   187	    rw [show (∑ a : G.AnswerA, (S.A x).effect a i.1 j.1) =
   188	        (1 : Op S.ιA) i.1 j.1 by
   189	      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.A x).sum_eq_one i.1) j.1]
   190	    rw [show (∑ b : G.AnswerB, (S.B y).effect b i.2 j.2) =
   191	        (1 : Op S.ιB) i.2 j.2 by
   192	      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.B y).sum_eq_one i.2) j.2]
   193	    exact congrFun (congrFun
   194	      (Matrix.one_kronecker_one (m := S.ιA) (n := S.ιB) (α := ℂ)) i) j
   195	  calc
   196	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b =
   197	        (inner ℂ S.ψ
   198	          (applyOperatorToState
   199	            (∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   200	              heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
   201	          simp [outcomeWeight, applyOperatorToState]
   202	    _ = (inner ℂ S.ψ (applyOperatorToState 1 S.ψ)).re := by rw [hsum]
   203	    _ = 1 := by
   204	      simp [applyOperatorToState, S.ψ_norm]
   205	
   206	/-- Summing over Bob's answers gives Alice's marginal Born weight. -/
   207	theorem sum_outcome_weight_right {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   208	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) :
   209	    (∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b) = aliceOutcomeWeight S x a := by
   210	  have hsum :
   211	      (∑ b : G.AnswerB, heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) =
   212	        heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1 := by
   213	    ext i j
   214	    simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
   215	      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
   216	    rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
   217	    rw [show (∑ b : G.AnswerB, (S.B y).effect b i.2 j.2) =
   218	        (1 : Op S.ιB) i.2 j.2 by
   219	      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.B y).sum_eq_one i.2) j.2]
   220	  calc
   221	    (∑ b : G.AnswerB, outcomeWeight S x y a b) =
   222	        (inner ℂ S.ψ
   223	          (applyOperatorToState
   224	            (∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   225	              heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
   226	          simp [outcomeWeight, applyOperatorToState]
   227	    _ = (inner ℂ S.ψ
   228	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1) S.ψ)).re := by
   229	      rw [hsum]
   230	    _ = aliceOutcomeWeight S x a := rfl
   231	
   232	/-- Summing over Alice's answers gives Bob's marginal Born weight. -/
   233	theorem sum_outcome_weight_left {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   234	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (b : G.AnswerB) :
   235	    (∑ a : G.AnswerA, outcomeWeight S x y a b) = bobOutcomeWeight S y b := by
   236	  have hsum :
   237	      (∑ a : G.AnswerA, heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) =
   238	        heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b) := by
   239	    ext i j
   240	    simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
   241	      Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
   242	    rw [← Finset.sum_mul]
   243	    rw [show (∑ a : G.AnswerA, (S.A x).effect a i.1 j.1) =
   244	        (1 : Op S.ιA) i.1 j.1 by
   245	      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun (S.A x).sum_eq_one i.1) j.1]
   246	  calc
   247	    (∑ a : G.AnswerA, outcomeWeight S x y a b) =
   248	        (inner ℂ S.ψ
   249	          (applyOperatorToState
   250	            (∑ a : G.AnswerA,
   251	              heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
   252	          simp [outcomeWeight, applyOperatorToState]
   253	    _ = (inner ℂ S.ψ
   254	        (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by
   255	      rw [hsum]
   256	    _ = bobOutcomeWeight S y b := rfl
   257	
   258	/-- Every answer event has nonnegative Born weight. -/
   259	theorem outcome_event_weight_nonneg {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   260	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   261	    (E : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] :
   262	    0 ≤ outcomeEventWeight S x y E := by
   263	  unfold outcomeEventWeight
   264	  exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => by
   265	    split_ifs
   266	    · exact outcomeWeight_nonneg S x y a b
   267	    · exact le_rfl
   268	
   269	/-- An answer event depending only on Alice has its Alice marginal weight. -/
   270	theorem outcome_event_weight_left_eq {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   271	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   272	    (E : G.AnswerA → Prop) [DecidablePred E] :
   273	    outcomeEventWeight S x y (fun a _ => E a) = aliceEventWeight S x E := by
   274	  unfold outcomeEventWeight aliceEventWeight
   275	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   276	  intro a _
   277	  by_cases ha : E a
   278	  · simp [ha, sum_outcome_weight_right S x y a]
   279	  · simp [ha]
   280	
   281	/-- An answer event depending only on Bob has its Bob marginal weight. -/
   282	theorem outcome_event_weight_right_eq {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   283	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   284	    (E : G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidablePred E] :
   285	    outcomeEventWeight S x y (fun _ b => E b) = bobEventWeight S y E := by
   286	  unfold outcomeEventWeight bobEventWeight
   287	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   288	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   289	  intro b _
   290	  by_cases hb : E b
   291	  · simp [hb, sum_outcome_weight_left S x y b]
   292	  · simp [hb]
   293	
   294	/-- Inclusion of answer events implies the corresponding Born-weight inequality. -/
   295	theorem outcome_event_weight_mono {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   296	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
   297	    (E F : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] [DecidableRel F]
   298	    (hEF : ∀ a b, E a b → F a b) :
   299	    outcomeEventWeight S x y E ≤ outcomeEventWeight S x y F := by
   300	  unfold outcomeEventWeight
   301	  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   302	  intro a _
   303	  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
   304	  intro b _
   305	  by_cases hE : E a b
   306	  · simp [hE, hEF a b hE]
   307	  · simp only [hE, ↓reduceIte]
   308	    split_ifs
   309	    · exact outcomeWeight_nonneg S x y a b
   310	    · exact le_rfl
   311	
   312	/--
   313	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   314	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   315	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   316	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   317	-/
   318	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   319	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
   320	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   321	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
   322	
   323	/--
   324	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
   325	strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
   326	for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
   327	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin

   329	intentionally not asserted here.

     4	/-!
     5	# Average lemmas for finite-support distributions
     6	
     7	This module contains the finite-sum and uniform-average lemmas for the project
     8	`Distribution` type.  The primitive distribution definitions, uniform
     9	distributions, and total variation distance live in
    10	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.Distribution`.
    11	
    12	## Main declarations
    13	
    14	The main results are the algebraic rules for `avgOver`, scalar and
    15	operator-valued forms of the module-valued finite-sum rules for uniform
    16	distributions, and the comparison between finite uniform averages and Mathlib
    17	uniform probability mass functions.
    18	
    19	## References
    20	
    21	These are formalization-internal finite probability lemmas for the low
    22	individual degree test development.

    29	/-! ### Averaging infrastructure
    30	
    31	Linearity proofs use `Distribution.weightedSumLinearMap`; order and support
    32	estimates use Mathlib's `Finset.sum` API. -/
    33	
    34	/-- Averaging the zero function gives zero. -/
    35	theorem avgOver_zero {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) :
    36	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun _ => 0) = 0 := by
    37	  simp [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap]
    38	
    39	/-- Averaging preserves order when weights are nonneg. -/
    40	theorem avgOver_mono {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f g : α → Error)
    41	    (hfg : ∀ a, f a ≤ g a) :
    42	    avgOver 𝒟 f ≤ avgOver 𝒟 g := by
    43	  simp only [avgOver]
    44	  exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hfg a) (𝒟.nonnegative a)
    45	
    46	/-- Averaging a nonneg function with nonneg weights gives a nonneg result. -/
    47	theorem avgOver_nonneg {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → Error)
    48	    (hf : ∀ a, 0 ≤ f a) :
    49	    0 ≤ avgOver 𝒟 f := by
    50	  simpa [avgOver_zero] using avgOver_mono 𝒟 (fun _ => 0) f hf
    51	
    52	/-- Averaging distributes over addition. -/
    53	theorem avgOver_add {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f g : α → Error) :
    54	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a + g a) =
    55	      avgOver 𝒟 f + avgOver 𝒟 g := by
    56	  change avgOver 𝒟 (f + g) = avgOver 𝒟 f + avgOver 𝒟 g
    57	  simpa [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap] using
    58	    map_add (𝒟.weightedSumLinearMap Error) f g
    59	
    60	/-- Averaging distributes over subtraction. -/
    61	theorem avgOver_sub {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f g : α → Error) :
    62	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a - g a) =
    63	      avgOver 𝒟 f - avgOver 𝒟 g := by
    64	  change avgOver 𝒟 (f - g) = avgOver 𝒟 f - avgOver 𝒟 g
    65	  simpa [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap] using
    66	    map_sub (𝒟.weightedSumLinearMap Error) f g
    67	
    68	/-- Averaging commutes with scalar multiplication. -/
    69	theorem avgOver_const_mul {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
    70	    (c : Error) (f : α → Error) :
    71	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => c * f a) =
    72	      c * avgOver 𝒟 f := by
    73	  change avgOver 𝒟 (c • f) = c • avgOver 𝒟 f
    74	  simp [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap, smul_eq_mul]
    75	
    76	/-- Averaging commutes with scalar multiplication on the right. -/
    77	theorem avgOver_mul_const {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
    78	    (f : α → Error) (c : Error) :
    79	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a * c) = avgOver 𝒟 f * c := by
    80	  unfold avgOver
    81	  calc
    82	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a * (f a * c)
    83	      = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, (𝒟.weight a * f a) * c := by
    84	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    85	          intro a _
    86	          ring
    87	    _ = (∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a * f a) * c := by
    88	          rw [Finset.sum_mul]

    90	/-- Pull a finite outcome sum through an average. -/
    91	theorem avgOver_sum {α β : Type*} [Fintype β]
    92	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → β → Error) :
    93	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => ∑ b : β, f a b) =
    94	      ∑ b : β, avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a b) := by
    95	  rw [show (fun a => ∑ b : β, f a b) = ∑ b : β, fun a => f a b by
    96	    ext a
    97	    simp]
    98	  simp [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap]

   100	/-- Pull a finite-set sum through an average. -/

   102	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (s : Finset β) (f : α → β → Error) :
   103	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => ∑ b ∈ s, f a b) =
   104	      ∑ b ∈ s, avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a b) := by
   105	  rw [show (fun a => ∑ b ∈ s, f a b) = ∑ b ∈ s, fun a => f a b by
   106	    ext a
   107	    simp]
   108	  simp [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap]

   110	/-- Fubini swap for two nested finite-support distribution averages. -/
   111	theorem avgOver_comm {α β : Type*} (𝒟α : Distribution α) (𝒟β : Distribution β)
   112	    (f : α → β → Error) :
   113	    avgOver 𝒟α (fun a => avgOver 𝒟β (f a)) =
   114	      avgOver 𝒟β (fun b => avgOver 𝒟α (fun a => f a b)) := by
   115	  unfold avgOver
   116	  simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   117	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   118	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   119	  intro b _
   120	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   121	  intro a _
   122	  ring

   124	/-- If `f = g` pointwise, their averages agree. -/
   125	theorem avgOver_congr {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   126	    (f g : α → Error) (h : ∀ a, f a = g a) :
   127	    avgOver 𝒟 f = avgOver 𝒟 g := by
   128	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => by rw [h a]

   134	    (f g : α → Error) (h : ∀ a, a ∈ 𝒟.support → f a = g a) :
   135	    avgOver 𝒟 f = avgOver 𝒟 g := by
   136	  simp only [avgOver]
   137	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha => by rw [h a ha]

   139	/-- Averaging preserves supportwise order when weights are nonnegative.  This is

   143	    avgOver 𝒟 f ≤ avgOver 𝒟 g := by
   144	  unfold avgOver
   145	  exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun a ha =>
   146	    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (h a ha) (𝒟.nonnegative a)
   147	
   148	/-- The average of a constant scalar is the total mass times that scalar. -/

   150	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun _ : α => c) =
   151	      (∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a) * c := by
   152	  unfold avgOver
   153	  rw [Finset.sum_mul]

   155	/-- Averaging a constant against a probability distribution returns that constant. -/

   158	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun _ : α => c) = c := by

   162	nonnegative pointwise upper bound. -/
   163	theorem avgOver_le_of_weight_sum_le_one {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)

   166	    (hδ_nonneg : 0 ≤ δ)
   167	    (hf : ∀ a, f a ≤ δ) :

   176	/-- Fixed left and right multiplications factor through an operator average. -/
   177	theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_mul_left_right {α : Type*}

   186	  intro a _

   188	
   189	/-- Averaging against a probabilistic project distribution is the finite sum
   190	over its stored support against the associated Mathlib probability mass

   193	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (f : α → Error) :
   194	    avgOver 𝒟 f = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a).toReal * f a := by
   195	  simpa [avgOver, smul_eq_mul] using
   196	    Distribution.sum_smul_eq_toPMF_support_sum 𝒟 h𝒟 f
   197	
   198	/-- Averaging against a probabilistic project distribution is the finite sum
   199	against its associated Mathlib probability mass function. -/
   200	theorem avgOver_eq_toPMF_sum {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
   201	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (f : α → Error) :
   202	    avgOver 𝒟 f = ∑ a : α, (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a).toReal * f a := by
   203	  simpa [avgOver, smul_eq_mul] using
   204	    Distribution.sum_smul_eq_toPMF_sum 𝒟 h𝒟 f
   205	
   206	/-- Averaging against a probabilistic project distribution is integration
   207	against its associated Mathlib probability mass function. -/
   208	theorem avgOver_eq_toPMF_integral {α : Type*}
   209	    [Finite α] [MeasurableSpace α] [MeasurableSingletonClass α]
   210	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (f : α → Error) :
   211	    avgOver 𝒟 f = ∫ a, f a ∂(𝒟.toPMF h𝒟).toMeasure := by
   212	  haveI := Fintype.ofFinite α
   213	  rw [avgOver_eq_toPMF_sum 𝒟 h𝒟 f, PMF.integral_eq_sum]

   215	
   216	/-- Operator-valued averaging against a probabilistic project distribution is
   217	the finite operator sum over the stored support against the associated Mathlib
   218	probability mass function. -/
   219	theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_eq_toPMF_support_sum {α : Type*}
   220	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability)
   221	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   222	    (f : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
   223	    averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 f =
   224	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a).toReal • f a := by
   225	  simpa [averageOperatorOverDistribution] using
   226	    Distribution.sum_smul_eq_toPMF_support_sum 𝒟 h𝒟 f
   227	
   228	/-- Operator-valued averaging against a probabilistic project distribution is
   229	the finite sum against its associated Mathlib probability mass function. -/
   230	theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_eq_toPMF_sum {α : Type*}
   231	    [Fintype α]
   232	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability)
   233	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

   235	    averageOperatorOverDistribution 𝒟 f =
   236	      ∑ a : α, (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a).toReal • f a := by

   238	    Distribution.sum_smul_eq_toPMF_sum 𝒟 h𝒟 f

   240	namespace Distribution.IsProbability
   241	
   242	/-- A supportwise upper bound also bounds the average of a probability distribution.
   243	This packages the paper convention that expectations are taken against genuine
   244	probability distributions, while still allowing `Distribution` itself to carry a
   245	larger ambient type than its explicit support. -/
   246	theorem avgOver_le_of_forall_le_on_support {α : Type*} {𝒟 : Distribution α}
   247	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (f : α → Error) (δ : Error)
   248	    (hf : ∀ a, a ∈ 𝒟.support → f a ≤ δ) :
   249	    avgOver 𝒟 f ≤ δ := by
   250	  calc
   251	    avgOver 𝒟 f ≤ avgOver 𝒟 (fun _ : α => δ) :=
   252	      avgOver_mono_on_support 𝒟 f (fun _ : α => δ) hf
   253	    _ = δ := avgOver_const_of_isProbability 𝒟 h𝒟 δ
   254	
   255	end Distribution.IsProbability
   256	
   257	/-- For two probability distributions, total variation is the total positive
   258	part of the signed weight difference `ν - μ`.
   259	
   260	This is the finite-distribution identity
   261	`(1 / 2) * ∑ |μ(a)-ν(a)| = ∑ max 0 (ν(a)-μ(a))`, written for the
   262	project `Distribution` representation. -/
   263	theorem totalVariationDistance_eq_sum_max_sub {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
   264	    (μ ν : Distribution α) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hν : ν.IsProbability) :
   265	    totalVariationDistance μ ν =
   266	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, max 0 (ν.weight a - μ.weight a) := by
   267	  classical
   268	  let u : Finset α := μ.support ∪ ν.support
   269	  have hμ_union :
   270	      ∑ a ∈ u, μ.weight a = 1 := by
   271	    apply hμ.weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset
   272	    intro a ha
   273	    exact Finset.mem_union_left ν.support ha
   274	  have hν_union :
   275	      ∑ a ∈ u, ν.weight a = 1 := by
   276	    apply hν.weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset
   277	    intro a ha
   278	    exact Finset.mem_union_right μ.support ha
   279	  have hdiff_sum :
   280	      ∑ a ∈ u, (ν.weight a - μ.weight a) = 0 := by

     4	/-!
     5	# The Magic Square game
     6	
     7	The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
     8	question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
     9	Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
    10	carrier is needed here.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, from
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	
    23	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    24	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 207-222, paper origin
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    26	-/
    27	inductive MsType where
    28	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    29	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    30	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    31	
    32	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    33	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
    34	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    35	-/
    36	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    37	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    38	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    39	
    40	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    41	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`; paper
    42	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    43	-/
    44	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    45	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    46	
    47	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    48	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
    49	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    50	-/
    51	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    52	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    53	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    54	
    55	/-- The Magic Square incidence graph has an edge, as required by the
    56	nonempty-support API of `graphDistribution`.  This is the finite carrier fact
    57	used to instantiate `def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`,
    58	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    59	-/
    60	theorem msEdges_nonempty : msEdges.Nonempty := by
    61	  refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.constraint 0) (.var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
    62	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(0, 0), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    63	
    64	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    65	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`,
    66	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    67	-/
    68	inductive MsAnswer where
    69	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    70	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    71	  deriving DecidableEq
    72	
    73	/-- A formalization-only total relabeling from the global Magic Square answer
    74	alphabet to a bit. It folds wrong-form answers into zero so that a variable
    75	question yields a complete binary measurement. -/
    76	def msBitOrZero : MsAnswer → ZMod 2
    77	  | .bit b => b
    78	  | .triple _ => 0
    79	
    80	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    81	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    82	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
    83	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    84	-/
    85	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    86	
    87	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
    88	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    89	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
    90	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    91	-/
    92	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    93	  toFun
    94	    | .triple β => .inl β
    95	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    96	  invFun
    97	    | .inl β => .triple β
    98	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    99	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   100	  right_inv := by
   101	    intro x
   102	    cases x <;> rfl
   103	
   104	noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
   105	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm
   106	
   107	instance : Inhabited MsAnswer := ⟨.bit 0⟩
   108	
   109	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
   110	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 207-222; paper
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`).
   112	-/
   113	def msWinPredicate :
   114	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   115	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   116	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   117	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   118	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   119	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   120	      decide
   121	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   122	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   123	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   124	      decide
   125	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   126	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   127	  | _, _, _, _ => false
   128	
   129	/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
   130	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
   131	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
   132	-/
   133	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   134	  QuestionA := MsType
   135	  QuestionB := MsType
   136	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   137	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   138	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty
   139	  μ_prob := by
   140	    apply Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability
   141	    refine ⟨(.constraint 0, .var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
   142	    simp [msEdges]
   143	  decide := msWinPredicate
   144	
   145	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-!
# Module-valued uniform finite sums for project distributions

This module contains the module-valued finite-sum algebra for the project
`Distribution` type.  The statements keep the paper-facing
`uniformDistribution` notation, but their proofs reduce the probability
calculation to the finite-expectation API for Mathlib probability mass
functions.

## Main declarations

* `Distribution.sum_smul_eq_toPMF_support_sum`
* `Distribution.sum_smul_eq_toPMF_sum`
* `uniformDistribution_sum_smul_eq_pmf_sum`
* `uniformDistribution_sum_smul_equiv`
* `uniformDistribution_sum_smul_prod`
* `uniformDistribution_sum_smul_comm`
* `uniformDistribution_sum_smul_prod_swap`
* `uniformDistribution_sum_smul_equiv_prod`
* `uniformDistribution_sum_smul_equiv_fst`
* `uniformDistribution_sum_smul_equiv_snd`
* `uniformDistribution_map_sum_smul_eq_uniform_of_factor_equiv`
* `uniformOnFinset_sum_smul_eq_subtype`
* `uniformOnFinset_filter_sum_smul_equiv`

## References

These are formalization-internal finite probability lemmas for the low
individual degree test development.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.LDT

namespace Distribution

/-- A module-valued finite weighted sum against a probabilistic project
distribution may be written with the real weights of the associated Mathlib
probability mass function, over the stored support. -/
theorem sum_smul_eq_toPMF_support_sum {α M : Type*}
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (f : α → M) :
    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f a =
      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a).toReal • f a := by
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => by
    rw [Distribution.toPMF_apply_toReal]

/-- A module-valued finite weighted sum against a probabilistic project
distribution may be written as a full finite sum with the real weights of the
associated Mathlib probability mass function. -/
theorem sum_smul_eq_toPMF_sum {α M : Type*} [Fintype α]
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (f : α → M) :
    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f a =
      ∑ a : α, (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a).toReal • f a := by
  rw [Distribution.sum_smul_eq_toPMF_support_sum 𝒟 h𝒟 f]
  exact (Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support 𝒟
    (fun a => (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a).toReal • f a)
    (by
      intro a ha
      rw [Distribution.toPMF_apply_of_notMem 𝒟 h𝒟 ha]
      simp)).symm

end Distribution

/-- Module-valued finite-sum expression for the uniform distribution, stated
without measurable-space assumptions. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_sum_smul_eq_pmf_sum {α M : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M] (f : α → M) :
    ∑ a ∈ (uniformDistribution α).support, (uniformDistribution α).weight a • f a =
      ∑ a : α, (PMF.uniformOfFintype α a).toReal • f a := by
  rw [Distribution.sum_smul_eq_toPMF_sum
    (uniformDistribution α) (uniformDistribution_isProbability α)]
  rw [uniformDistribution_toPMF]

/-- A finite-support uniform weighted sum is the corresponding Mathlib uniform
PMF-weighted sum. -/
theorem uniformOnFinset_sum_smul_eq_pmf_sum {α M : Type*}
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
    (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : α → M) :
    ∑ a ∈ (Distribution.uniformOnFinset s).support,
        (Distribution.uniformOnFinset s).weight a • f a =
      ∑ a ∈ s, (PMF.uniformOfFinset s hs a).toReal • f a := by
  rw [Distribution.sum_smul_eq_toPMF_support_sum
    (Distribution.uniformOnFinset s)
    (Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability s hs)]
  rw [Distribution.uniformOnFinset_support, Distribution.uniformOnFinset_toPMF]

/-- A constant family has uniform module-valued average equal to that constant.
This is the project-distribution form of `PMF.sum_const_smul`. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_sum_smul_const {α M : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M] (x : M) :
    ∑ a ∈ (uniformDistribution α).support, (uniformDistribution α).weight a • x = x := by
  rw [uniformDistribution_sum_smul_eq_pmf_sum]
  exact PMF.sum_const_smul (PMF.uniformOfFintype α) x

/-- Reindex a uniform module-valued average along an equivalence. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_sum_smul_equiv {α β M : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
    (e : α ≃ β) (f : α → M) :
    ∑ a ∈ (uniformDistribution α).support, (uniformDistribution α).weight a • f a =
      ∑ b ∈ (uniformDistribution β).support,
        (uniformDistribution β).weight b • f (e.symm b) := by
  rw [uniformDistribution_sum_smul_eq_pmf_sum (α := α)]
  rw [uniformDistribution_sum_smul_eq_pmf_sum (α := β)]
  simpa [PMF.realWeightedSum] using
    PMF.realWeightedSum_uniformOfFintype_equiv (e := e) (f := f)

/-- Split a uniform module-valued average over a product into iterated uniform
module-valued averages. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_sum_smul_prod {α β M : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
    (f : α → β → M) :
    ∑ ab ∈ (uniformDistribution (α × β)).support,
        (uniformDistribution (α × β)).weight ab • f ab.1 ab.2 =
      ∑ a ∈ (uniformDistribution α).support, (uniformDistribution α).weight a •
        ∑ b ∈ (uniformDistribution β).support,
          (uniformDistribution β).weight b • f a b := by
  rw [uniformDistribution_sum_smul_eq_pmf_sum (α := α × β)]
  rw [uniformDistribution_sum_smul_eq_pmf_sum (α := α)]
  simp_rw [uniformDistribution_sum_smul_eq_pmf_sum (α := β)]
  simpa [PMF.realWeightedSum] using
    PMF.realWeightedSum_uniformOfFintype_prod (f := f)

/-- Swap two nested uniform module-valued averages over finite nonempty types. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_sum_smul_comm {α β M : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
    (f : α → β → M) :
    ∑ a ∈ (uniformDistribution α).support, (uniformDistribution α).weight a •
        ∑ b ∈ (uniformDistribution β).support, (uniformDistribution β).weight b • f a b =
      ∑ b ∈ (uniformDistribution β).support, (uniformDistribution β).weight b •
        ∑ a ∈ (uniformDistribution α).support,

theorem outcome_event_weight_nonneg {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)
    (E : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop) [DecidableRel E] :
    0 ≤ outcomeEventWeight S x y E := by

    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)

    outcomeEventWeight S x y (fun a _ => E a) = aliceEventWeight S x E := by
  unfold outcomeEventWeight aliceEventWeight

    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)

    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB)

    (hEF : ∀ a b, E a b → F a b) :

  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
  intro a _
  apply Finset.sum_le_sum

  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)

strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested

intentionally not asserted here.

noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=

import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.DistributionAvg
import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.TensorPlacement
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.MagicSquareTheorems.Basic

/-!
# Magic Square value-to-parity relations

This file extracts the elementary probability relations used at the start of
the Magic Square rigidity argument.  A strategy of value at least `1 - ε` has
total rejection mass at most `ε`.  Since the question distribution is
supported on at most 36 directed incidences, the rejection mass at each
incidence is at most `36 * ε`.  This controls malformed answers, consistency
of the two reported bits at every cell, and the parity product on each of the
six row or column constraints.

The arguments apply to arbitrary finite POVMs.  In particular, malformed
answers remain in the event masses when `msBitOrZero` and
`constraintBitOrZero` turn the common answer alphabet into binary outcomes.

## References

The Magic Square game is defined in
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`

/-! ## The directed incidence distribution -/

/-- The 36 possible directed constraint-variable incidences. -/
def directedIncidence : ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool) → MsType × MsType
  | ((i, k), false) => (.constraint i, .var (msConstraintVars i k))
  | ((i, k), true) => (.var (msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i)

/-- Every question pair in the Magic Square distribution is a directed incidence. -/
theorem ms_support_subset_directedIncidences :
    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support ⊆
      (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).image directedIncidence := by
  intro xy hxy
  have hedge : Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges :=
    (Finset.mem_filter.mp hxy).2
  rcases Finset.mem_image.mp hedge with ⟨ik, _hik, heq⟩
  have heq' :
      ((.constraint ik.1, .var (msConstraintVars ik.1 ik.2)) : MsType × MsType) = xy ∨
        ((.constraint ik.1, .var (msConstraintVars ik.1 ik.2)) : MsType × MsType) =
          xy.swap :=
    (Sym2.mk_eq_mk_iff (α := MsType)).mp heq
  rcases heq' with heq' | heq'
  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(ik, false), Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    simpa [directedIncidence] using heq'
  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(ik, true), Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    simpa [directedIncidence] using congrArg Prod.swap heq'

/-- The Magic Square question distribution has at most 36 support points. -/
theorem ms_support_card_le :
    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card ≤ 36 := by
  calc
    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card ≤
        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).image
          directedIncidence).card :=
      Finset.card_le_card ms_support_subset_directedIncidences
    _ ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).card :=
      Finset.card_image_le
    _ = 36 := by norm_num

/-- A constraint-to-variable incidence belongs to the question support. -/
theorem ms_forward_incidence_mem_support (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    (.constraint i, .var (msConstraintVars i k)) ∈
      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support := by
  apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
  refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, k), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩

/-- A variable-to-constraint incidence belongs to the question support. -/
theorem ms_reverse_incidence_mem_support (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    (.var (msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i) ∈
      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support := by
  apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
  refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
  rw [Sym2.eq_swap]
  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, k), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩

/-- Every supported question pair has probability at least `1 / 36`. -/
theorem ms_question_weight_ge {xy : MsType × MsType}
    (hxy : xy ∈ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support) :
    (1 : ℝ) / 36 ≤ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy := by
  have hmemFilter :
      xy ∈ ((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
        Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges) := hxy
  rw [show (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy =
      1 / ((graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card : ℝ) by
    change (Distribution.uniformOnFinset
        ((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
          Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges)).weight xy =
      1 / (((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
        Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges).card : ℝ)
    rw [Distribution.uniformOnFinset_weight, if_pos hmemFilter]]
  apply one_div_le_one_div_of_le
  · exact_mod_cast Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨xy, hxy⟩
  · exact_mod_cast ms_support_card_le

/-! ## Born masses and events -/

/-- The Born mass of an answer pair conditioned on a question pair. -/
noncomputable def outcomeMass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType)
    (a b : MsAnswer) : ℝ :=
  (inner ℂ S.ψ
    (applyOperatorToState
      (heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)) S.ψ)).re

/-- Every conditioned answer-pair mass is nonnegative. -/
theorem outcomeMass_nonneg (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) (a b : MsAnswer) :
    0 ≤ outcomeMass S x y a b := by
  unfold outcomeMass applyOperatorToState
  have hpos :
      (Matrix.toEuclideanLin
        (heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b))).IsPositive := by
    rw [Matrix.isPositive_toEuclideanLin_iff]
    exact Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp
      (kronecker_nonneg ((S.A x).pos a) ((S.B y).pos b))
  change 0 ≤ RCLike.re (inner ℂ S.ψ
    ((Matrix.toEuclideanLin
      (heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b))) S.ψ))
  exact hpos.re_inner_nonneg_right S.ψ

/-- The answer-pair masses conditioned on fixed questions sum to one. -/
theorem outcomeMass_sum (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) :
    (∑ a : MsAnswer, ∑ b : MsAnswer, outcomeMass S x y a b) = 1 := by
  let A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement MsAnswer S.ιA := S.A x
  let B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement MsAnswer S.ιB := S.B y
  change (∑ a : MsAnswer, ∑ b : MsAnswer,
    (inner ℂ S.ψ
      (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect b)) S.ψ)).re) = 1
  calc
    (∑ a : MsAnswer, ∑ b : MsAnswer,
        (inner ℂ S.ψ
          (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect b)) S.ψ)).re) =
        (inner ℂ S.ψ
          (applyOperatorToState
            (∑ a : MsAnswer, ∑ b : MsAnswer,
              heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect b)) S.ψ)).re := by

   512	\subsection{The Magic Square game}
   513	\label{sec:ms}
   514	
   515	We recall the \emph{Magic Square game} of Mermin and
   516	Peres~\cite{mermin1990simple,peres1990incompatible,aravind2002simple}.
   517	The Magic Square game is a simple self-test for EPR pairs (it tests for two of
   518	them). In addition, it allows one to test that a pair of observables
   519	\emph{anticommutes}.
   520	Here we use it as a building block to construct the quantum low-degree test. 
   521	
   522	There are several formulations of the Magic Square game; here we present it as a
   523	\emph{binary constraint satisfaction} game~\cite{cleve2014characterization}.
   524	In this formulation of the game (denoted by $\game_\MS$) there are $6$ linear
   525	equations defined over $9$ variables that take values in $\F_2$.
   526	The variables correspond to the cells of a $3 \times 3$ grid, as depicted in
   527	Figure~\ref{fig:ms}.
   528	Five of the equations correspond to the constraint that the sum of the variables
   529	in each row and the first two columns must be equal to $0$, and the last
   530	equation requires that the sum of the variables in the last column must be equal
   531	to $1$.
   532	
   533	\begin{figure}[ht!]
   534		\begin{center}
   535	    \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.6}
   536			\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
   537				\hline
   538				$x_1$ & $x_2$ & $x_3$ \\
   539				\hline 
   540				$x_4$ & $x_5$ & $x_6$ \\	
   541				\hline
   542				$x_7$ & $x_8$ & $x_9$ \\
   543				\hline
   544			\end{tabular}
   545			\caption{The Magic Square game}
   546			\label{fig:ms}
   547			\end{center}
   548	\end{figure}
   549	
   550	The question set $\type^\ms$ of the Magic Square game is the following:
   551	\begin{equation*}
   552	  \begin{split}
   553	    \type^\msc & = \{ \Constraint_i : i = 1, 2, \ldots, 6\}\;,\\
   554	    \type^\msv & = \{ \Variable_j : j = 1, 2, \ldots, 9\}\;,\\
   555	    \type^\ms & = \type^\msc \cup \type^\msv\;.
   556	  \end{split}
   557	\end{equation*}
   558	The questions $\Constraint_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ correspond to the three row
   559	constraints, the questions $\Constraint_4$, $\Constraint_5$ correspond to the first
   560	two column constraints, and question $\Constraint_6$ corresponds to the third
   561	column constraint.
   562	
   563	In the Magic Square game, the verifier first samples a constraint $\Constraint_i
   564	\in \type^\msc$ uniformly at random, and then samples $\Variable_j$, one of the
   565	three variables in the row or column corresponding to $\Constraint_i$, uniformly
   566	at random.
   567	One player is randomly assigned to be the $\Constraint$ player, and the other is
   568	assigned to be the $\Variable$ player.
   569	The $\Constraint$ player is sent the question $\Constraint_i$ and is expected to
   570	respond with three bits $(\beta_{v_1}, \beta_{v_2}, \beta_{v_3}) \in \F_2^3$,
   571	where $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ are the indices of the three variables corresponding to
   572	$\Constraint_i$.
   573	The $\Variable$ player is given question $\Variable_j$ and is expected to
   574	respond with a single bit $\gamma \in \F_2$.
   575	The players win if the $\Constraint$ player's answers satisfy the equation
   576	associated with $\Constraint_i$, and $\gamma = \beta_j$.
   577	More precisely, the verifier samples an edge of the type graph (see Section~\ref{sec:types}) $G^\ms$
   578	in Fig.~\ref{fig:type-graph-ms}, sends one endpoint to a random player, and the
   579	other endpoint to the other player.

   612	The following theorem records the self-testing (also known as \emph{rigidity})
   613	properties of the Magic Square game.
   614	Its self-testing properties
   615	are crucial to the Pauli basis test.
   616	In particular, it is used to enforce anticommutation relations between certain
   617	pairs of operators.
   618	We will refer to this theorem in the proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test (\Cref{thm:pauli} below) in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}.
   619	
   620	\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]
   621	  \label{thm:ms-rigidity}
   622	
   623	
   624	Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\game^{\MS}$ with probability $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ is a state. Then there exist local isometries $\phi_A: \mH_A \to \mH_{A'} \otimes \mH_{A''},\phi_B: \mH_B \to \mH_{B'} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ (where $\mH_{A'},\mH_{B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\otimes 2}$ and $\mH_{A''},\mH_{B''}$ are finite dimensional) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{A''} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ such that 
   625	\begin{enumerate}
   626	    \item $\left \| \phi_A \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2} \otimes \ket{\aux} \right \| \leq O(\sqrt{\eps})$,
   627	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have that
   628	    \begin{gather*}
   629	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^X_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   630	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^Z_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   631	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^X_b)_{B'} \\
   632	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^Z_b)_{B'}
   633	    \end{gather*}
   634	    where the $\approx_{\sqrt{\eps}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}_{A'B'} \otimes \ket{\aux}_{A''B''}$ and the answer summation is over $b \in \{0,1\}$. As a consequence, letting 
   635	    \begin{gather*}
   636	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_1 \\
   637	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_1 \\
   638	    \end{gather*}
   639	    it holds that
   640	    \begin{gather*}
   641	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} \otimes I_{B' B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \otimes I_{B' B''} \\
   642	        I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \;,
   643	      \end{gather*}
   644	      where the notation $M \approx_{\delta} N$ for $M, N$ that are not POVM
   645	      elements means
   646	      \[  \bra{\psi} (M-N)^\dagger (M-N) \ket{\psi}  \leq  O(\delta). \]
   647	\end{enumerate}
   648	
   649	\end{theorem}
   650	\begin{proof}
   651	 	A proof of the rigidity of the Magic Square game can be found in~\cite[Theorem 6.9]{coladangelo2017robust}. There are a couple minor differences between their rigidity statement and the one stated here. First, they state that the robustness of the Magic Square self-test is $O(\eps)$; however they specify the closeness between the actual and ideal states in terms of the trace norm, whereas we specify the closeness between $\phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi}$ and $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}\otimes \ket{\aux}$ in terms of the Euclidean distance, which translates to $O(\sqrt{\eps})$ instead of $O(\eps)$. Second, their choice of ideal strategy specifies that the observables corresponding to $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$ questions are $I \otimes \sigma^Z$ and $\sigma^{Z} \sigma^{X} \otimes \sigma^Z \sigma^X$; however under a local change of basis these are equivalent to $\sigma^X \otimes I$ and $\sigma^Z \otimes I$ respectively.
   652	\end{proof}

/-!
# Uniform subset estimates

This file contains estimates for the total variation distance between the
uniform distribution on a finite type and the uniform distribution on a
nonempty finite subset, together with averaging bounds for `[0,1]`-valued
functions.  The uniform-subset total-variation identity is proved by transport
through Mathlib probability mass functions.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- Total variation between the uniform distribution on a finite ambient type and
the uniform distribution on a nonempty finite subset.

This is the elementary finite identity
`TV(uniform α, uniform s) = 1 - |s| / |α|`.  The proof transports the project
`Distribution` statement to Mathlib's uniform probability mass functions. -/
theorem totalVariationDistance_uniformDistribution_uniformOnFinset_eq
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty) :
    totalVariationDistance (uniformDistribution α) (Distribution.uniformOnFinset s) =
      1 - (s.card : Error) / (Fintype.card α : Error) := by
  rw [totalVariationDistance_eq_toPMF_sum]
  change PMF.totalVariationDistance
      ((uniformDistribution α).toPMF (uniformDistribution_isProbability α))
      ((Distribution.uniformOnFinset s).toPMF
        (Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability s hs)) =
    1 - (s.card : Error) / (Fintype.card α : Error)
  rw [uniformDistribution_toPMF, Distribution.uniformOnFinset_toPMF]
  exact PMF.totalVariationDistance_uniformOfFintype_uniformOfFinset_eq s hs

/-- A `[0,1]`-valued function averaged over a nonempty finite subset is bounded
by its ambient uniform average plus the total variation distance between the
two uniform distributions. -/
theorem avgOver_uniformOnFinset_le_uniformDistribution_add_totalVariationDistance
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty)
    (f : α → Error)
    (hf_nonneg : ∀ a, 0 ≤ f a)
    (hf_le_one : ∀ a, f a ≤ 1) :
    avgOver (Distribution.uniformOnFinset s) f
      ≤ avgOver (uniformDistribution α) f
        + totalVariationDistance (uniformDistribution α) (Distribution.uniformOnFinset s) := by
  exact
    avgOver_le_avgOver_add_totalVariationDistance
      (uniformDistribution α) (Distribution.uniformOnFinset s)
      (uniformDistribution_isProbability α)
      (Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability s hs)
      f hf_nonneg hf_le_one

end MIPStarRE.LDT

# Conditionally linear functions and graph distributions

The question distributions in the Pauli basis test are generated by a finite
graph of types and a shared seed, with each type applying a conditionally linear
map to that seed.  The inductive predicate below records the level structure

The source-facing nodes are `def:cl-func`, `def:cl-dist`, `lem:cl-concat`, and
`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-535`.
The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`
and `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1010`.
-/

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

/--
The source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive
predicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is
rejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same
public predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together
with its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation
deviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes
`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
-/
inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
  | succ {ell : ℕ}
      (S₁ : Finset ι)
      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)

/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary
coordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,
blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
-/
def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0

/-- Evaluation of a conditionally-linear syntax term.  Lean-only support for
`def:cl-func`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
-/
def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0
  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>
      fun x =>
        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x
        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x

/-- The support invariant for a conditionally-linear syntax term.  This is a
Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
-/
def CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
  | _, .zero, _ => True
  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)

/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
-/
def IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,
    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S ∧ CondLinearTerm.eval t = L

/--
`IsCondLinear` abbreviates the full-coordinate predicate.  Blueprint
`def:cl-func`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`; paper
`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
-/
def IsCondLinear (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
  IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L
